 Scotland Under-20s’ build up for age-grade Six Nations gathers pace
 Head coach Fergus Pringle has named a 33 player training squad ahead of pre-Christmas clashes against Ireland then Wales By David Barnes | 12 November 2026 | Scotland Rugby , Youth Scotland Rugby , Youth Henry Widdowson has been named in the 33 player Scotland Under-20s squad ahead of next Friday's match against Ireland in Cork. Image: © Craig Watson - www.craigwatson.co.uk SCOTLAND Under-20s will play two ‘matches against Ireland in Cork next Friday (20th November) and Wales at home in mid-December, ahead of the age-grade Six Nations kicking off in February, with head coach Fergus Pringle having selected a 33-player squad (listed below) for the first of those games. 
 There are 16 players involved who had a role in the U20s Six Nations, Junior World Championship or June warm-up fixtures last season. They are forwards Archie Appleby, Christian Lindsay, Daniel Cruickshanks, Harry Jackaman, Harvey Preston, Jack Utterson, Jackson Rennie and Rory Baxter , and backs  Adam McKenzie, Callum Jessop, Dan Kelly, Harry Clark, Harry Soboil, Henry Kesterton, Henry Widdowson and Rory McHaffie. 
 There are three exiles in the squad, whose names have been removed from this article for the time being as we have been advised that they’re involvement is not yet confirmed.

 Loading... Among the other notable new faces are props Michael Scarth (Currie Chieftains) and Murray Robertson (Edinburgh Accies), who emerged out of Orkney via Glanalmond College last season.
 Zak Burgess , who is initially from Stonehaven but now playing for GHA whilst being in the West National Talent Pathway, can operate at both loose-head and tight-head.
 Murray Robertson , also of Edinburgh Accies, has played predominantly at inside-centre this season, but is also comfortable at full-back and stand-off.

 19 Comments
 DAVID McAdam on 14 November 2026 at 12:44 pm An good looking squad for this stage of the season. It will be augmented come the new year; some people will not be available just now because of injury, or university commitments etc. Others will emerge through the training opportunities. In regard to Angus Robson – he started the season very well at Watsons, then had a concussion injury; maybe he is working his way back to fitness with Strathclyde Uni while the Premiership is on its rest weeks for the IDC and therefore doesn’t have games. It is not that unusual for players to combine University/club games to tailor their fitness and opportunities. There are usually one or two players emerge from BUCS Premier 1 rugby as we turn the corner into the new year, often to add bulk to the pack. And last year Jake Dalziel emerged very late in the Autumn to cement the starting position at 10. It wouldn’t be a surprise if Xander Sneddon did the same this year – still U18 he might very well be propelled into the U20 backline somewhere.
 Reply 
 CFD on 12 November 2026 at 11:48 pm Zak Burgess from Stonehaven!? He played alongside my son at Greenock Wanderers for years, before moving up the road to GHA for u18’s.
 1 Reply 
 David Simpson on 12 November 2026 at 12:21 pm Hadn’t realised Kesterton, McHaffie and Kelly all had another year at u20s. All 3 look like they could be really good. Ditto Jack Utterson but if he’s going to be a hooker he needs to play there! The ongoing absence of Jessop from the Academy structure baffles me, he’s looked good every time I’ve seen him play and you don’t get a game at fly half at 18 in the Prem unless you’ve got something about you.
 3 Reply Lalalala Lamb on 12 November 2026 at 1:20 pm Is this the Callum Jessop who’s listed in the squad that you’re referring to, or is there another?
 1 Reply Lalalala Lamb on 12 November 2026 at 1:25 pm Meant to expand on the post above, apologies.
 I believe that Callum Jessop is involved in the National Talent Pathway already, he just hasn’t been assigned to one of the Pro Teams yet. But he has played in one or two Edinburgh A games so they clearly have an eye on him.
 1 Reply David Simpson on 13 November 2026 at 10:58 am He’s not listed as being in the NTP above.
 1 Reply Toonie's Advisor on 13 November 2026 at 2:16 pm NTP is 3 stages – U17, U18 & U19. After that you need to get an academy contract or find you own way in the world. Jessop is now an U20 year age so NTP no longer an option. However, it baffles me that he isn’t an Edinburgh academy player.
 2 
 Leicester Boy on 12 November 2026 at 2:55 pm He was also starting 10 for Edinburgh District last Friday night. Talented player, good boot and pace!
 3 Reply 
 CFD on 12 November 2026 at 10:19 pm Re. Jessop. Baffling absentees from the Academies/Scotland u20 squad is nothing new! A few years back Glasgow Hawks’ 1st XV top try scorer was an 18 year old winger. Remember he scored two tries and got man off the match in a Prem game with the 20’s coach looking on. At no point was he even invited to a training session to have a look at him, while u20 players from Hawks 2nd XV were called up.
 Reply 
 David B on 16 November 2026 at 1:30 pm I think he’s studying at Uni, which probably precludes being a full part of the Academy set up
 Reply 
 Iain Rae on 12 November 2026 at 12:03 pm Good luck to all selected and hopefully Fergus and his team can build on the good performances in Georgia
 2 Reply 
 Craig Malloch on 12 November 2026 at 9:29 am I think there’s a typo in last paragraph should be Finlay Anderson not Murray Robertson unless Murray is particularly versatile?!
 4 Reply 
 Page on 12 November 2026 at 6:15 am Is Dan Robson injured or just not considered ready? Seen he’s not been in the last couple of Watsonians squads.
 Decent looking squad with a fair few who performed well last year. Presumably a few more exiles to be added come 6N.
 I also saw a combined academies group trained for a week with Bordeux then beat the Espoirs team. It seems like the youngsters are getting a few more games recently though a bit haphazardly. I’d love tonsee some analysis at some point across the u20s, academy squads, and fringe youngsters to see whether it really has improved over the last few years.
 4 Reply Toonie's Advisor on 12 November 2026 at 12:39 pm Do you mean Angus Robson (10)? think he is playing Uni rugby
 1 Reply Page on 12 November 2026 at 2:56 pm Sorry, yep, that’s him, don’t know where I got Dan from! Strange for him to shift across to uni rugby at this stage if that’s the case.
 1 Reply OV on 12 November 2026 at 3:24 pm Not really, I don’t think, especially if he’s not going to uni in Edinburgh.
 The reality is that the chances of making it as a professional rugby player are pretty slim, and even if you do make it, it’s a relatively short career, so you still need to think about what comes afterwards.
 I do think it’s a shame, though, because I genuinely think he’s the best age-grade 10 we have. But it’s fairly obvious the SRU already worship at the altar of another 10!
 10 1 Reply Page on 12 November 2026 at 5:50 pm Yeah, not suggesting at all he shouldn’t go to uni. Just assumed as he is in the NTP that would mean they would have him playing as high a level of rugby as possible. Of course, depending on where he has gone to uni, the rugby might be pretty high level so might be a win win.
 3 
 Lalalala Lamb on 13 November 2026 at 10:21 am I have to admit to finding your last paragraph somewhat strange.
 First of all, this is a training squad, not the final squad for the U20 Six Nations. So it’s entirely possible that Robson along with any other missing players will be in the tournament squad still.
 Second of all, why are you negatively talking in riddles about another 10? If you are talking about one of the stand-offs in this squad, both fully deserve their chances and have played very well for Heriots/Edinburgh District and Edinburgh ‘A’ this season respectively.
 If you are referring to the incumbent stand-off from the U20 World Championship, I hope you’ll notice that he is not in this squad either. He is however getting starts for a professional Premiership team in England, so clearly isn’t that bad of a player either.
 Thirdly, the seemingly passive-aggressive way you’re writing about ‘another 10’ is a bit harsh on the lad himself whichever one you’re referring to. Just because you personally prefer Robson to him doesn’t mean you need to be talking negatively about a young lad who is only doing his best.
 2 1 
 Alistair on 12 November 2026 at 10:02 pm Edinburgh have played five A games largely consisting of academy players, against decent sides from England and Ireland, plus the combined trip to Bordeaux.
 So at least in the east it hasn’t been haphazard – they’ve had games to play every week or two.
 I’m not sure what Glasgow has organised, but I assume they’ve been arranging games for their academy players too.
